# Extensions sevenx_multisite activates

This page is for administrators and hosts who need to know which extensions a `sevenx_multisite` install switches
on, and for developers who add one. It answers: which extensions are listed, in which order, which ones are only
active in the administration, and how their tables are created.

## Contents

1. [Where the list lives](#where-the-list-lives)
2. [The list, in order](#the-list-in-order)
3. [Why the order matters](#why-the-order-matters)
4. [Extensions of the administration only](#extensions-of-the-administration-only)
5. [Extensions the installer checks for](#extensions-the-installer-checks-for)
6. [Extension tables](#extension-tables)

## Where the list lives

`initSettings()` in `settings/sevenx-multi-site-installer.php` stores the list as the setting `extension_list`.
`commonSiteINISettings()` writes it to `settings/override/site.ini.append.php` as
`[ExtensionSettings] ActiveExtensions`. The same list is used during the install itself: `preInstall()` adds the
`settings/` folder of each listed extension to the running configuration (`activateSiteExtensionSettings()`), so their
datatypes and INI files are known while the packages are imported.

> **Warning**
> The extensions must be present in `extension/` of the installation; the package does not bring them. A listed
> extension that is missing is simply not found at run time.

## The list, in order

| # | Extensions | Notes from the installer |
|---|---|---|
| 1 | `xrowmetadata` | the metadata datatype many classes use |
| 2-3 | `expui`, `ezjscore` | Exponential UI before ezjscore, so its settings (jQuery 4, the admin's script and style lists) win |
| 4 | `expservices` | remote services for admin apps and JavaScript front ends; its portal designs get no siteaccess |
| 5 | `expqueue` | the job queue (Setup > Job queue); its worker runs with the admin siteaccess from cron |
| 6 | `ezoracle` | the Oracle driver, "inert on any other database" |
| 7-9 | `ezoe`, `ezformtoken`, `ezwt` | the online editor, cross site request forgery protection for posted forms, the website toolbar |
| 10-16 | `ezstarrating`, `ezgmaplocation`, `ezautosave`, `ezodf`, `ezie`, `ezprestapi`, `ezpaypal` | |
| 17-18 | `owsimpleoperator`, `swark` | template operators |
| 19-21 | `bcgooglesitemaps`, `bcwebsitestatistics`, `bccie` | |
| 22-24 | `xrowextract`, `enhancedezbinaryfile`, `enhancedselection2` | `enhancedselection2` owns the `sckenhancedselection` datatype of several `ng_*` classes |
| 25 | `birthday` | the ezbirthday datatype |
| 26-27 | `ezwebin`, `ezmultiupload` | |
| 28 | `syndication` | content syndication between installations |
| 29-30 | `ezupdate`, `git_manager` | |
| 31-32 | `eztags`, `ngclasslist` | |
| 33-44 | `explayouts`, `explayouts_core`, `explayouts_api`, `explayouts_standard`, `explayouts_site_api`, `explayouts_relation_list_query`, `explayouts_tags_query`, `explayouts_content_browser_core`, `explayouts_content_browser`, `explayouts_content_browser_ui`, `explayouts_ui`, `explayouts_ui_api` | the layouts family, "the providers ... listed before the UI that consumes them" |
| 45-48 | `expquery_translator`, `expsite_core`, `expsite_api`, `expsite_app` | |
| 49-51 | `exp_enhanced_link`, `expchangeclass`, `ezownerchange` | `ezownerchange` changes the owner of an object or a subtree |
| 52 | `cjw_newsletter` | its classes and tree are imported by a post-install step |
| 53-54 | `recaptcha`, `hcaptcha` | `hcaptcha` "needs its keys set" |
| 55 | `sevenx_authentication_2fa` | two-factor and social login |
| 56-57 | `powercontent`, `sevenx_dse` | |
| 58-59 | `sevenx_themes_media`, `sevenx_themes_simple` | the two themes, kept at the end |
| 60 | `ezurlmultisite` | links to content of the other site point at the siteaccess that serves it |

## Why the order matters

The comment above the list explains it: "Order matters: later extensions win design and template overrides, so the
two themes stay at the end." When a datatype is looked up, "the first match wins", which is why
`activateSiteExtensionSettings()` adds the settings folders in the order the site will load them
(`eZExtension::extensionOrdering()` is applied when `[ExtensionSettings] ExtensionOrdering=enabled`).

> **Tip**
> To add an extension to the default install, add it to `extension_list` in the place its settings need, and check
> whether it has tables (see below). The extension history of the installer shows the pattern: "activates
> ezownerchange" (2026-10-15), "activates ezurlmultisite with the node ids of the new installation" (2026-10-14).
> See [Changing the installer script](../your-own/changing-the-installer-script.md).

## Extensions of the administration only

Three extensions are deliberately not in `extension_list`. `adminAccessExtensionList()` returns `expai`,
`exp_adminui` and `sqliimport`, each only when `extension/<name>` exists, and `adminSiteINISettings()` writes them as
`[ExtensionSettings] ActiveAccessExtensions` of the admin siteaccess. The editor and adminui siteaccesses are copies
of the admin's files and inherit them, except that the setup step makes the editor without `sqliimport`.

- `expai` (Exponential Intelligence) "installs switched off: its own [AISettings] Enabled=false, no provider key is
  written". Its cron part needs the admin siteaccess.
- `exp_adminui` makes Admin UI a choice of the design menu in the admin and editor; "every other siteaccess keeps its
  own design".
- `sqliimport` (imports, with schedules on the expqueue worker) needs `expqueue` and `expui`, which are in
  `extension_list`. Its 13 tables come from `extensionSchemas()`, its **Imports** tab sits between Export and CIE in
  the admin's tab list, and only the Administrator role has its policies. Its schedules run from cron every minute
  with the admin siteaccess: `php runcronjobs.php -q -s <admin> expqueue` and `php runcronjobs.php -q -s <admin>
  sqliimport`.

## Extensions the installer checks for

| Extension | What the installer does when it is present |
|---|---|
| `sevenx_authentication_2fa` | adds the "Two-step sign-in" field to the user class, writes `sevenxauthentication2fa.ini` (`Enforce2FA=enabled` with `EnforcedGroups[]` Administrator users and Editors, so their members set up a second step at their first sign-in while every other account chooses for itself; `DefaultMethod=totp`, `RecoveryCodes=10`, no exemptions, no grace period, a `SecretKey` made for this installation), sets `LoginHandler` `sevenxUser2fa` then `standard`, and gives `user2fa/setup` and `user2fa/verify` to Member, Editor and Partner |
| `cjw_newsletter` | imports its content classes into the class group "Newsletter", creates the newsletter tree and sets its root folder setting |
| `exp_adminui` | creates the `adminui` siteaccess |
| `ezurlmultisite` | writes `settings/override/ezurlmultisite.ini.append.php` (see [What you have after installing](what-you-have-after-installing.md)) |
| `explayouts` | imports the default admin layouts from `share/fragments/admin_layouts_db_data.dba` |

## Extension tables

`extensionSchemas()` decides which extensions get their tables during `preInstall()`:

1. The extensions named by hand in `declaredExtensionSchemas()`, in this order: `sevenx_themes_media` (schema and
   data), `ezstarrating`, `ezgmaplocation`, `eztags`, `explayouts` (schema and data), `enhancedselection2`,
   `cjw_newsletter`, `syndication`.
2. Every other extension of `extension_list`, and `expai` and `exp_adminui`, that ships a `share/db_schema.dba` or a
   `sql/<engine>/schema.sql` (schema only).

`dropExtensionTables()` first drops every table those schemas declare, because a reinstall's database "remove" drops
only tables named `ez*` and "the others kept the previous site's rows". `insertDBFile()` then creates each schema
through `eZDbSchema`, skipping tables an earlier schema of the same run already created, and falls back to
`sql/<engine>/` files on a database without an `eZDbSchema` handler. `createMissingSchemaTables()` creates any table
the schema insert left out. What this means for the layout data is on
[Layouts data and the share .dba files](layouts-data-and-share-dba.md).
